events.title: Athenians defeat the Persians at Marathon
events.description: By the traditional date, the Athenians and Plataeans charged and routed the Persian landing force at Marathon. The legend of a runner carrying news to Athens inspired the modern marathon race.
events.html: By the traditional date, the Athenians and Plataeans charged and routed the Persian landing force at Marathon. The legend of a runner carrying news to Athens inspired the modern marathon race.

events.title: Simon de Montfort defeats and kills Peter II of Aragon at Muret
events.description: Crusaders under Simon de Montfort routed a larger army of Aragon and Toulouse at Muret, killing King Peter II. The defeat ended Aragonese hopes in Languedoc and opened it to northern French rule.
events.html: Crusaders under Simon de Montfort routed a larger army of Aragon and Toulouse at Muret, killing King Peter II. The defeat ended Aragonese hopes in Languedoc and opened it to northern French rule.

events.title: John III Sobieski relieves the siege of Vienna
events.description: A relief army led by King John III Sobieski of Poland routed the Ottoman forces besieging Vienna, ending with a great charge of Polish hussars. The Ottoman advance into central Europe was halted for good.
events.html: A relief army led by King John III Sobieski of Poland routed the Ottoman forces besieging Vienna, ending with a great charge of Polish hussars. The Ottoman advance into central Europe was halted for good.

events.title: Switzerland adopts its federal constitution
events.description: The Swiss Diet declared the new federal constitution accepted, turning a loose league of cantons into a federal state with a two-chamber parliament. Its framework still underpins Switzerland today.
events.html: The Swiss Diet declared the new federal constitution accepted, turning a loose league of cantons into a federal state with a two-chamber parliament. Its framework still underpins Switzerland today.

events.title: Kennedy tells Rice University 'we choose to go to the Moon'
events.description: In a speech at Rice University in Houston, John F. Kennedy committed America to a Moon landing that decade, 'not because they are easy, but because they are hard'. Apollo 11 landed seven years later.
